title: Integrated Primary Care Model for Youth Substance Use Disorders
implementation_guidance: Implement an integrated primary care model for adolescents and young adults with substance use disorders; establish a multidisciplinary team including primary care, addiction treatment, mental health, and social services; screen all youth for substance use using validated tools (CRAFFT, S2BI); provide same-day access when possible; offer medications for opioid use disorder when indicated; incorporate harm reduction strategies including naloxone distribution; address co-occurring mental health conditions through integrated behavioral health services; develop proactive re-engagement strategies for youth who miss appointments; create flexible scheduling options; establish clear protocols for managing polysubstance use; coordinate with community resources for housing and other social needs.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of substance use disorders, increased engagement in treatment, enhanced retention in care, reduced substance-related harms, better management of co-occurring mental health conditions, improved coordination of care, increased access to evidence-based treatments, reduced barriers to care.
target_population: Medicaid-enrolled adolescents and young adults (ages 14-26) with substance use disorders or problematic substance use, particularly those with co-occurring mental health conditions or housing instability.
citation: Bagley SM, Hadland SE, Schoenberger SF, et al. Integrating substance use care into primary care for adolescents and young adults: Lessons learned. J Subst Abuse Treat. 2021;129:108376. doi:10.1016/j.jsat.2021.108376
